metadata.title: Optimal Algorithms for Distributed Optimization

extraction_notes.note: Tables 1 and 2 (iteration-complexity comparison and summary of the four cases) are not extracted; their entries restate the case theorems and cited rates.
definition or claim: one sentence both introduces the dual function, mu_phi and L_phi and asserts its strong convexity and smoothness; kept as definition since the symbols are used throughout.
Section 8 restates ClP2 and ClP3 combined; kept as its own claim rather than an also_stated_at copy because it merges two statements.
The optimality claim for all four cases is one sentence; the following sentences comparing with centralized FGM bounds plus consensus cost were taken as its prose proof.

metadata.extraction_comment: Many results in Sections 5-9 are stated in prose with only citation-level justification; they are claims with rigor semi_formal.

nodes.statement: resizeboxcolumnwidth! |c|C1.5cm|c|c|c|c| hline bf Approach &multicolumn1|C1.5cm|Reference & multicolumn1|C2.7cm|mu-strongly convex and L-smooth & multicolumn1|C2.2cm|mu-strongly convex and mboxM-Lipschitz & multicolumn1|C1.5cm|L-smooth & multicolumn1|C2.1cm|mboxM-Lipschitz \\ hline Centralized & & tildeOleft( sqrtfracLmu right) &tildeOleft( fracM^2mu varepsilon right) & tildeOleft( sqrtfracLvarepsilon right) & tildeOleft( fracM^2varepsilon^2right) \\hline multirow7*parbox[c]1.5cm Primal & &tilde Oleft( left( fracLmu right) ^5/7m^3right) & - & tilde Oleft( frac1varepsilon^5 / 7right)^*** & -\\ & & tildeOleft( m^2 + sqrtfracLmumright) & -& oleft( frac1varepsilonright) & oleft( frac1varepsilonright)^** \\ & & - & -& -& tildeOleft( fracM^2mvarepsilon^2right) \\ & & tildeOleft( fracLmum^2right) &- & - & - \\ & & -&- & tildeOleft( fracL varepsilon m^3right) & - \\ & & tildeOleft( fracLmum^4right) &- & tildeOleft( fracL varepsilon m^4right) &-\\ & & tildeOleft( sqrtfracLmum^2right)^**** & & & \\ hline multirow2*parbox[c]1.5cm Dual Friendly &^* & tildeOleft( sqrtfracLmum right) & - & - & -\\ &This paper^*& tildeOleft( sqrtfracLmum right) &tildeOleft( sqrtfracM^2mu varepsilon mright) & tildeOleft( sqrtfracL varepsilon mright) & tildeOleft( fracMvarepsilonmright) \\ hline multicolumn6Lcolumnwidth^* The function F(x) is assumed dual friendly. hspace7cm ^** Additionally, it is assumed functions are proximal friendly. hspace7cm^*** An iteration complexity of tildeO(sqrt1 / varepsilon ) is shown if the objective is the composition of a linear map and a strongly convex and smooth function. hspace6cm ^**** A linear dependence on m is achieved if L is sufficiently close to mu. captionIteration Complexity of Distributed Optimization Algorithms. The iteration complexity refers to the required number of oracle calls. For distributed algorithms based on primal iterations this translates to computations of gradients of the local functions for each of the agents. On the other side, for dual based algorithms, the complexity refers to computations of the gradient of the Lagrange dual function, which in translates to the number of communication rounds in the network.

nodes.statement: Chebyshev acceleration is suggested in , where instead of using the interaction matrix W one can analyze the algorithm with a different one P_K(W). P_K(W) is a polynomial of degree K, and its eigengap is maximized with a specific choice based on Chebyshev polynomials. If K is chosen as sqrtchi(W) then mboxchileft( P_sqrtchi(W)(W)right) sim 1.
nodes.raw_latex: Chebyshev acceleration is suggested in \cite{sca17}, where instead of using the interaction matrix $W$ one can analyze the algorithm with a different one $P_K(W)$. $P_K(W)$ is a polynomial of degree $K$, and its eigengap is maximized with a specific choice based on Chebyshev polynomials.
